images.filename: Istanbul Eyüp Mihrişah Sultan complex Mausoleum entrance from street 3907.jpg
images.caption: One of some pictures taken in or of the mausoleum (türbe) of the complex, or of other parts of this element in the complex. Apart from her mausoleum there are other elements in a baroque complex (külliye) founded (1794) by Mihrişah Valide Sultan, mother of Selim III. There is a mektep or primary school, its portico is situated along the east side of the courtyard with the mausoleum. There also is, further east along the street with the opening to the courtyard, an imaret (public kitchen) along three sides of another courtyard. And further east there is a sebil.
images.alt: One of some pictures taken in or of the mausoleum (türbe) of the complex, or of other parts of this element in the complex. images.caption:
1911 multilingual Ottoman calendar page from Thessaloniki:

The upper left shows the Rumi date in Ottoman Turkish: year 1327, Nisan 7 (٧ نیسان ١٣٢٧)
The same Julian date (7 April, ΑΠΡΙΛΙΟΣ 7) and day (Thursday, Πέμπτη) appears below in Greek with the AD year 1911
Next to that is the Gregorian date (20 April, AVRIL 20) and day (Jeudi) in French
Above these two is the number 30 (twice, purpose unclear probably because the relevant month is 30 days), the month April, (Априлий) and day (Thursday, Четвъртъкъ) in Bulgarian
Under the Greek is Armenian, reading April (ԱՊՐԻԼ, april) and Thursday (ՀԻՆԳՇԱԲԹԻ, hingšabtʿi)
The upper right shows the Islamic date 21 Rebiülahir 1329 (١٣٢٩ ربيع الآخر ١٢)
The Hebrew date 22 Nisan 5671 (22 ‏ניסן‎ 5671) appears at the bottom, mentioning Thursday (in Ladino language) and Pesach (גﬞוגיבﬞיס פסח).
